title: Two finite ordered Cech comparisons for a flasque resolution
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $e:F[0]\to G^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism of nonnegative cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose each $G^q$ has flasque underlying abelian sheaf [def-sc-zariski-flasque]. Let $(V_i)_{0\leq i<r}$ be a finite open cover of $X$, allowing $r=0$ when $X$ is empty. For each nonempty subset $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$ put $V_S=\bigcap_{i\in S}V_i$, and suppose the section augmentation $\Gamma(V_S,F)[0]\to\Gamma(V_S,G^\bullet)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For $p,q\geq0$ define $L^p=\prod_{|S|=p+1}\Gamma(V_S,F)$ with the alternating restriction differential. Define the commuting double complex $D^{p,q}=\prod_{|S|=p+1}\Gamma(V_S,G^q)$, with horizontal alternating restriction differential and vertical resolution differential, with all terms zero outside $p,q\geq0$, and total differential $d_h+(-1)^p d_v$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Then the two cochain maps $\alpha:\Gamma(X,G^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ and $\beta:L^\bullet\to\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ are quasi-isomorphisms, where $\alpha$ is restriction into the $p=0$ summands and $\beta$ is the section map of $e$ into the $q=0$ summands. Their degree-zero composites with $\Gamma(X,F)\to\Gamma(X,G^0)$ and with $\Gamma(X,F)\to L^0$ agree. These component-defined maps commute with coefficient maps, restriction to open subsets carrying the restricted cover, and a scheme morphism $h:Y\to X$ with the inverse-image indexed cover $h^{-1}V_i$, whenever supplied $\mathcal O_X$-linear coefficient and cochain resolution maps $F\to h_*F'$ and $G^\bullet\to h_*G'^\bullet$ commute with augmentations (where $F'$ and $G'^\bullet$ are the coefficient sheaf and resolution on $Y$). The quasi-isomorphism assertion on $Y$ assumes the same flasqueness and section-augmentation hypotheses there. No flatness of $h$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent cochain-level formulation of Tag 09SZ (lemma-flasque-acyclic-cech) and Tag 01ET (lemma-cech-spectral-sequence-application), using the canonical double-complex maps in Tag 01EQ (lemma-cech-cohomology) and the ordered complex of Tag 01FJ (lemma-ordered-alternating), together with Tag 01FM (lemma-alternating-usual), the ordered/usual homotopy equivalence; all labels in cohomology.tex.

proof.text: Work throughout in abelian groups, or in modules over $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ by restriction of scalars. Write each subset in increasing order. In the alternating face sum, terms deleting positions $i<j$ occur twice with signs $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ and $(-1)^{i+j}$, so the horizontal differential squares to zero. Restrictions commute with the resolution differential, hence $d_hd_v=d_vd_h$. The total differential is therefore the one specified in the statement. Restriction of a global section has horizontal differential zero (the two restrictions to every overlap agree), and commutes with $d_v$. Thus $\alpha$ is a cochain map. For $\beta$, the equation $d_G^0e^0=0$ kills the vertical part and restriction naturality of $e^0$ gives the horizontal cochain identity. These arguments also apply when an indexed product is empty, hence zero.

source.place: Tag 01EQ (lemma-cech-cohomology), component maps; Tag 01FJ (lemma-ordered-alternating), alternating faces

proof.text: We prove directly that for any flasque abelian sheaf $A$ and any finite ordered family of opens, its ordered section complex has zero positive cohomology; the family need only cover its own union. Induct on the number $r$ of opens, simultaneously for every space and every flasque sheaf. For $r=0$ the complex is zero; for $r=1$ all positive terms are zero. For $r>1$ let $a$ be a degree-$k$ cocycle, $k>0$, and put $j=r-1$. By induction the restriction of $a$ to subsets avoiding $j$ equals $db$ for a degree-$(k-1)$ cochain of the first $r-1$ opens. Extend $b$ to the full complex by setting all components containing $j$ to zero, and replace $a$ by $a-db$. The new cocycle is zero on all subsets avoiding $j$. For $W_i=V_i\cap V_j$, $i<j$, put $t_T=a_{T\cup\{j\}}$, for $|T|=k$. Evaluating $da=0$ on $R\cup\{j\}$ gives $d_Wt=0$: the last face is zero and the other faces have precisely the ordered differential signs. If $k>1$, induction on the $r-1$ opens $W_i$ for the restriction of $A$ to $V_j$ gives $t=d_Wu$. This restriction is flasque because its restriction maps are those of $A$. Define $c_{R\cup\{j\}}=u_R$ for $|R|=k-1$, and set $c$ to zero on subsets avoiding $j$. Then $(dc)_{T\cup\{j\}}=(d_Wu)_T=t_T$, and all other components are zero, so the residual $a$ is $dc$. If $k=1$, the equation $d_Wt=0$ says that the $t_i$ agree on overlaps. Sheaf gluing produces $t$ over $W=\bigcup_{i<j}W_i\subseteq V_j$. Flasqueness extends $t$ to $s\in A(V_j)$. Take $c_j=s$ and $c_i=0$ for $i<j$; then $(dc)_{i,j}=s|_{W_i}=t_i$ and all other components vanish. This again gives $dc=a$. Adding back the first $b$ proves exactness. Empty intersections and an empty $W$ use $A(\varnothing)=0$, which follows from the sheaf axiom for the empty cover.

source.place: Tag 09SZ (lemma-flasque-acyclic-cech), finite ordered variant proved here by induction, with ordered differential as in Tag 01FJ

proof.text: For a finite cover of $X$, a degree-zero ordered Cech cocycle is a tuple $(s_i)$ with $s_i|_{V_i\cap V_j}=s_j|_{V_i\cap V_j}$. The sheaf gluing and uniqueness axioms identify these tuples with $A(X)$ via restriction. There are no degree-zero boundaries. Together with Step 2, for every $q$ the augmented horizontal row $\Gamma(X,G^q)[0]\to D^{\bullet,q}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. If $r=0$, the covering condition implies $X=\varnothing$, so both its source and target are zero by the empty-cover sheaf axiom.

Let $B^{0,q}=\Gamma(X,G^q)$ and $B^{p,q}=0$ for $p\ne0$, with vertical differential the section differential. Restriction is a double-complex map $f:B\to D$ by Step 1. In the explicit hypothesis of the cited theorem, $K.\mathrm{flip}.X(q)$ is the horizontal complex $K^{\bullet,q}$ (the outer index of $K$ is $p$). Thus its required maps for $f$ are exactly $\Gamma(X,G^q)[0]\to D^{\bullet,q}$, proved quasi-isomorphisms in Step 3. Apply that theorem directly, without flipping $f$, in the abelian category of abelian groups. Both bicomplexes are first quadrant, so every total degree has finitely many summands; there is no upper bound required on the resolution degree. The resulting total map is precisely $\alpha$, since its only source summand in degree $n$ is $(0,n)$, the differential there is $d_v$, and its components are restrictions. Hence $\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01EQ (lemma-cech-cohomology), augmented-row argument; Homology Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), via the cited column-comparison theorem

proof.text: For each fixed $p$, the augmentation $L^p[0]\to D^{p,\bullet}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. To verify finite-product preservation here without another lemma, cycles in a product complex are exactly tuples of cycles, and boundaries are exactly tuples of boundaries: a tuple of boundary elements has a tuple of preimages, chosen over the finite set of subsets $S$. Therefore cohomology is the product of the cohomologies and its augmentation map is the product of the stipulated section-augmentation isomorphisms. The product over an empty set is zero. Put $E^{p,0}=L^p$ and $E^{p,q}=0$ for $q\ne0$, with horizontal differential $d_L$. The augmentation defines a double-complex map $g:E\to D$ by Step 1. Flip both indices: the horizontal rows of $E^{\mathrm{flip}}\to D^{\mathrm{flip}}$ are exactly the original vertical column maps just checked. These are the maps in the cited theorem's explicit flipped-component hypothesis, so that theorem gives a quasi-isomorphism on the flipped totals. Identify each flipped total with the original total by multiplying the summand originally indexed $(p,q)$ by $(-1)^{pq}$. For a horizontal arrow, the flipped differential followed by this sign has coefficient $(-1)^q(-1)^{(p+1)q}=(-1)^{pq}$; for a vertical arrow the coefficient is $(-1)^{p(q+1)}=(-1)^{pq}(-1)^p$. These are exactly the coefficients of $d_h+(-1)^pd_v$ after applying the source sign. Hence this is a cochain isomorphism. It commutes with $g$ because $g$ preserves both indices and the signs are identical on source and target. The resulting original total map is a quasi-isomorphism. Since $\operatorname{Tot}(E)=L^\bullet$ and the sign on its $q=0$ summands is one, this map is precisely $\beta$.

source.place: Tag 01ET (lemma-cech-spectral-sequence-application), acyclic-column argument for the given resolution; Homology Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution)

proof.text: For $s\in\Gamma(X,F)$, both degree-zero composites have $i$-th component $e^0(s)|_{V_i}=e^0(s|_{V_i})$ in $D^{0,0}$. Thus the composites agree. For naturality, write $u:F\to h_*F^{\prime}$ and $v:G^\bullet\to h_*G^{\prime\bullet}$ for the supplied maps. On each subset $S$, the induced component maps are $u_{V_S}$ and $v^q_{V_S}$, with target sections over $h^{-1}V_S=\bigcap_{i\in S}h^{-1}V_i$. Their sheaf-morphism identities give $v^q_{V_T}\operatorname{res}_{S,T}=\operatorname{res}^{\prime}_{S,T}v^q_{V_S}$ for $S\subset T$, their cochain identities give $d_{G^{\prime}}v^q=v^{q+1}d_G$, and their augmentation identity gives $v^0e^0=e^{\prime0}u$. Summing the first equality with the same ordered face signs proves compatibility with $d_h$; the second proves compatibility with the signed vertical differential, and the third gives the $\beta$ square. Evaluating the first equality on $X\supseteq V_i$ gives the $\alpha$ square. Coefficient maps are the case $h=1_X$, and restriction to an open $W$ is the case of its inclusion with the indexed family $(W\cap V_i)$. No inverse-image exactness, flatness or preservation of flasqueness is used. On $Y$ repeat Steps 1--5 only when the stated hypotheses there hold. All displayed maps are additive and semilinear over the global structure-ring map, which suffices for the asserted naturality.
